messages.subject: add matrix to plot using facet_plot
messages.subject_clean: add matrix to plot using facet_plot
messages.body_plain:
I would like to plot a matrix such as p6 in the below code using facet_plot in ggtree, I am attempting to do this in p5 but am stuck

any ideas?

library(ggstance)
library(ggtree)
library(reshape)

tr <- rtree(30)
p <- ggtree(tr)
p <- p + geom_tiplab(size=3) + xlim_tree(4)
d1 <- data.frame(id=tr$tip.label, location=sample(c("GZ", "HK", "CZ"), 30, replace=TRUE))
p1 <- p %<+% d1 + geom_tippoint(aes(color=location))
d2 <- data.frame(id=tr$tip.label, val=rnorm(30, sd=3))
p2 <- facet_plot(p1, panel="dot", data=d2, geom=geom_point,
                 aes(x=val), color='firebrick') + theme_tree2()

d3 <- data.frame(id = rep(tr$tip.label, each=2),
                 value = abs(rnorm(60, mean=100, sd=50)),
                 category = rep(LETTERS[1:2], 30))
p3 <- facet_plot(p2, panel = 'Stacked Barplot', data = d3,
                 geom = geom_barh,
                 mapping = aes(x = value, fill = as.factor(category)),
                 stat='identity' )

p4 <- facet_plot(p1, panel="my bar", data=d3, geom=geom_barh,
                 mapping = aes(x = value, fill = as.factor(category)),
                 stat='identity' )  + theme_tree2()

m <- 30
n <- 15
m1 <- as.data.frame(matrix(sample(0:1, m * n, replace = TRUE), m, n))

m1$id <- tr$tip.label

m2 <- melt(m1[,c(ncol(m1),1:(ncol(m1)-1))])

p5 <- facet_plot(p3, panel="my matrix", data=m2, geom=geom_point,
                 mapping = aes(x = value))  + theme_tree2()

p6 <- ggplot(m2, aes(x = variable, y = id)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill=value)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low="white", high="red")

messages.subject_clean: add matrix to plot using facet_plot
messages.body_plain:
see https://github.com/GuangchuangYu/ggtree/issues/82.
facet_plot(p2, panel='matrix', data=m2, geom=geom_tile, aes(x=as.numeric(variable), fill=value))

If you want to use p3, the same issue happened, as fill = as.factor(category) in p3, and now you want to fill = value for m2, and it will throw the following error:
Error: Continuous value supplied to discrete scale

If the m2$value is binary, you need to convert it to factor and it will work smoothly.
facet_plot(p3, panel='matrix', data=m2, geom=geom_tile, aes(x=as.numeric(variable), fill=as.factor(value)))
​

messages.subject: collapsed nodes as triangles
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I've looked all over google and the vingettes, but I can't seem to find a way to show collapsed nodes as triangles.

I often want to collapse a subtree that is not of interest, but show it as a triangle to indicate that the collapsed node contains many taxa.

See attached PDF where I've used TreeGraph2 to collapse Animals and Plants in this tree of life. Is there any way to replicate this look in ggtree?

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: collapsed nodes as triangles
messages.body_plain:
A rightward facing triangle is available as a UTF-8 character, 9668.

To using the collapse manipulator from collapse clade <https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/ggtree/inst/doc/treeManipulation.html#collapse-clade>, you can then annotate the tip with the triangle as a geom_text2. You will need to change the hjust and vjust to adjust position and the cex to make it the right size. For example, if you wanted to collapse node 232 from the example bird.families dateset from ape:

library(ggtree)
library(ape)
data(bird.families)
coll <- ggtree(bird.families) + geom_tiplab(cex=1.2) + xlim(0,70) + ylim(0,130)
coll <- coll %>% collapse(node=232)
coll <- coll + geom_text2(aes(subset=(node == 232)), cex=2, label=intToUtf8(9668), hjust =.2,vjust=.45)
coll <- coll + geom_text2(aes(subset=(node == 232)), cex=1.5, vjust=0.2, label="Group",hjust = -.5)
coll

The collapse() manipulator also shortens the tree, which makes it impossible to represent how many taxa are included in the group. There would also be a way to collapse while preserving shape by grouping with OTUs, but that would get really complicated quite quickly. Easier to just do it manually if you have many collapsed nodes.

If you any other questions, don't forget to include some reproducible code by using the rtree() function, or the bird.families dataset.

messages.subject: Adding internal nodes to facet_plot
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I wonder if there is any way to associate data with internal nodes of a phylogenetic tree in addition to its tips as in function `facet_plot`.

The possible solution may be to introduce additional tips corresponding to the internal nodes, thus making the tree ternary:

```

library(ggtree)

tr <- read.tree(text='(((Tip1,NodeA,Tip2),((Tip3,NodeB,Tip4),Tip5,NodeC),NodeD), Tip6, NodeE);')

p <- ggtree(tr) + geom_tiplab(align=TRUE) + xlim_tree(5)

png('tip_node_plot.png', 640, 640)

plot(p)

dev.off()

```

An example of the produced figure is attached.

However, this solution has two drawbacks: first, internal nodes can be shown on the top or the bottom of the subtree instead of being in the middle (for example, NodeD); second, lines from internal tips to the corresponding nodes might be broken (for example, NodeC).

Best regards,

Gaik
